title: Modulo-eight nonvanishing at every odd Lemire endpoint
statement: For every integer ell at least one, the number I_(2ell+1)(1) of monic irreducible binary polynomials of degree 2ell+1 congruent to 1 modulo x^(ell+1) is not divisible by eight. THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE: ell=27 gives I_55(1)=4883944, which is divisible by eight.

evidence.supports: At ell=27 the exact uniqueness-bounded transform gives N_55(1)=268616921 and I_55(1)=4883944=0 mod 8, refuting the universal statement.
evidence.notes: Fleet replay on s4 exited zero after 4217.201 seconds at 30417756 KiB peak RSS. Executable SHA-256 0a505ec4360069c868999d5c00819f2e31721d83fbfc8086e27f56ad4d3cea2; complete output/timing-log SHA-256 1567140e8a0875ab55514ddacb8d114c235818a0dcea2830b1e5ffc4906e7744. The single NTT residue is admitted only because a proved candidate-count bound makes it the unique integer result.

provenance.source: exact uniqueness-bounded odd-endpoint transform on s4

notes: The first 25 exact rows, through degree 51, were nonzero modulo eight and had two-adic valuation at most two. The declared stopping row ell=27, degree 55, has valuation three and refutes the universal claim. The same witness contains 4883944 requested irreducibles, so it does not refute Lemire existence. Deuring-Shafarevich still gives two-rank zero for the associated Carlitz cover, and the exact primitive-character Newton polygons remain valid diagnostics, but neither implies fixed-modulus nonvanishing.
